successCriteria.description: The Employee entity extends BaseEntity and is exported from the employee module's barrel (index.ts); it compiles under strict TypeScript with no implicit any.

IEmployeeRepository declares all seven operations — findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByEmail, findByManagerId, findAll, create, update — each returning the specified Promise<Employee | null>, Promise<Employee[]>, or Promise<Employee> type.
PgEmployeeRepository implements IEmployeeRepository and obtains its database connection from the shared pg pool in src/shared/db/connection.ts (no separate Pool construction inside the module).
create persists a new employee row and returns an Employee whose id, createdAt, and updatedAt are populated (not the caller-supplied input shape).
update applies a partial update to an existing employee and returns the updated Employee, or returns null when no row matches the given id.
findById, findByEmployeeNumber, and findByEmail return null when no matching row exists; findByManagerId and findAll return an empty array when no rows match.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts mock the pg pool and assert each CRUD path: create, read by id/employeeNumber/email/managerId, findAll, update, and the not-found (null/empty) cases.
The phase passes the mechanical verification gate: npm run build (tsc) succeeds with no type errors and npx jest runs the employee repository tests green.

constraints: All database access goes through the repository pattern (GP-001); PgEmployeeRepository is the only component in this phase that touches the pg pool — no inline SQL outside the repository.
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks; use unknown with type guards instead of any (HARNESS no-any rule).

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the employee module must not import another module's internals, and downstream consumers must import Employee/IEmployeeRepository/PgEmployeeRepository via src/modules/employee/index.ts.
No unhandled promise rejections (GP-006): every async repository method must surface errors via rejected promises or typed error handling rather than throwing synchronously out of an async boundary.
Test files must follow the project Jest convention: *.test.ts under tests/ (testMatch '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)'); do not use .spec.ts or alter jest.config.js.
No hardcoded secrets (HARNESS no-hardcoded-secrets); the repository must consume the shared pool whose connection string comes from DATABASE_URL, not a locally constructed connection.
outOfScope: Employee service, controller, and routes (employee.service.ts, employee.controller.ts, employee.routes.ts) — this phase covers only the model, repository interface, repository implementation, and barrel.
Audit record writing for employee create/update (GP-002) — no audit module exists yet; audit integration is deferred to the leave orchestration phase that wires GP-002.
RBAC enforcement on employee operations (GP-005) — there is no controller/route layer in this phase; RBAC is applied at the API boundary in a later phase.
Input validation at API boundaries (GP-003) — no API boundary exists in this phase; the repository accepts already-shaped Employee data.
Database migrations / schema creation for the employees table — this phase assumes the employees table exists per the reconciled architecture; migrations are out of scope.
Soft-delete (deleted_at) handling and delete operations — PLAN.md lists no delete method on IEmployeeRepository and the field list omits deletedAt; deletion is deferred.

ambiguities.description: PLAN.md specifies department as a non-null string, but DOMAIN.md lists department as string | null (required=false). The reconciled architecture lists it as a plain string. The Employee model's nullability for department is ambiguous.
options: department: string (non-null, per PLAN.md and reconciled.json)

ambiguities.description: PLAN.md types employmentStatus as a plain string; DOMAIN.md and the reconciled schema constrain it to the union 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' | 'TERMINATED'. The model's type for employmentStatus is ambiguous.

The employees table schema in the reconciled architecture and DOMAIN.md includes a deleted_at column (soft delete), but PLAN.md's Employee field list omits deletedAt and BaseEntity has no deletedAt. Whether the Employee model exposes a deletedAt field is ambiguous.
options: Omit deletedAt from the Employee model (match PLAN.md field list + BaseEntity); soft-delete is a DB-only concern
Include deletedAt: Date | null on the Employee model (match DOMAIN.md and DB schema)

ambiguities.description: PLAN.md says import BaseEntity from ../../shared/types/base-entity.interface, but the module-boundary rule (AGENTS.md / ARCHITECTURE.md) requires modules to import shared types through the shared barrel (src/shared/types/index.ts). The correct import path for BaseEntity is ambiguous.
options: Import BaseEntity from ../../shared/types (barrel, per module-boundary rule)

entityInvariants.invariant: Employee extends BaseEntity, so every Employee instance carries id (string), createdAt (Date), and updatedAt (Date) in addition to its own domain fields; the create operation must populate these three rather than accept them from the caller.

managerId is nullable (string | null): an employee with no manager is a valid state and must be representable; downstream leave-approval logic escalates managerless employees to HR admin rather than rejecting them.
terminationDate is nullable (Date | null): an actively employed employee has a null terminationDate; a non-null terminationDate indicates the employee is no longer active.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no row matches; rejects the promise on a pool/query error (no unhandled rejection — GP-006).
Returns null when no row matches; rejects on query error.
Returns null when no row matches; rejects on query error.
Returns an empty array (not null) when no direct reports exist; rejects on query error.
Returns an empty array when the table has no rows; rejects on query error.
Accepts an Employee minus id/createdAt/updatedAt; returns a fully-populated Employee; rejects on a unique-constraint violation (duplicate employeeNumber or email) or query error.
Applies a partial update and returns the updated Employee, or returns null when no row matches the id; rejects on query error.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The Employee entity must extend the existing BaseEntity interface exactly as defined (id: string, createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date) — do not redefine or widen those three fields.
PgEmployeeRepository must obtain its database connection from the shared `pool` exported by src/shared/db/connection.ts rather than constructing its own pg.Pool.

The Employee entity shape must match the reconciled architecture's Employee domain entity (employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus plus BaseEntity fields); surface — do not silently diverge from — any difference between PLAN.md and the reconciled schema.

The repository unit test must be placed at a path matching testMatch '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)' (i.e. tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts) and run under the existing ts-jest preset without modifying jest.config.js.

If BaseEntity is imported via the shared barrel rather than the deep path, the barrel must already re-export BaseEntity (it does: `export type { BaseEntity } from './base-entity.interface'`); the chosen import path must resolve against this existing export.

integrationPoints.why: Employee extends BaseEntity; this is the declared Phase 1 dependency the phase explicitly depends on.
PgEmployeeRepository consumes the shared pool for all database access (GP-001 repository pattern; no direct Pool construction).
Downstream phases (balance, leave) import Employee and IEmployeeRepository only through this barrel per the module-boundary rule; it must re-export all three symbols.

The leave orchestration phase depends on IEmployeeRepository.findByManagerId and findById to resolve the submitter/approver manager hierarchy and the managerless-escalation rule; this phase establishes that contract.
